observedFacts.frame: One shared unboxed Cartesian frame. Positive horizontal arrow at source right and positive vertical arrow at source top. No negative signs, no grid, no subpanels.
observedFacts.ticks: Exactly five downward temperature ticks labelled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; raster centers x=93,128,162,195,231. Retain these positions, not an invented uniform grid.
observedFacts.labels: Vertical Greek rho, an origin 0, and horizontal T with historical degree-K notation; there are no numbered rho ticks and no vertical unit. Modern label T (K) removes obsolete degree notation without changing Kelvin.
observedFacts.zero: Visible zero-rho branch coincides with the horizontal baseline up to the abrupt transition. Its left end is the visible axis-origin clipping boundary, not a measured lower temperature cutoff. No marker or temperature numeral is added there.
observedFacts.transition: The narrow nearly vertical ink stripe occupies x=198..203 continuously through the baseline; representative centerline x=201 runs from y=286 to the adjoining upper shoulder y=211. It is just to the right of tick 4, before tick 5. These are raster locations, not inferred rho numbers or an exact calibrated transition temperature.
observedFacts.trace: Solid upper branch rises to the right with increasing slope. Every integer source column 208..455 is measured as the midpoint of its contiguous ink run. First center is (208,211); terminal nonempty column is (455,37), with x=456 and x=457 empty. No extrapolation, fitted physical function, marked samples, rho values or upper endpoint temperature is added.
observedFacts.historical: The full current text explicitly attributes 4.1 K to the original historical mercury report; it does not define a universal critical temperature. The figure does not add a 4.1 tick or modern numerical correction.

modernAdditions: Translation only: source x + 23 and source screen y + 104; top/bottom white margins are enlarged for 32px labels.
Source baseline scanner skew (about y286 left to y282 right) is leveled to y286, and its vertical axis is straightened; tick x centers and upper-curve coordinates are not rescaled or regularized.
Variable strokes are normalized to semantic ink axes and semantic accent data trace. Labels are typeset rather than copied raster handwriting.
T (K) is the modern notation for the source Kelvin axis. Mercury (original report) is a text-bound provenance qualifier, not an additional source label.
